nodes.summary: If an ω-language $L$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$ is recognized by a finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton, so is its complement $\Sigma^\omega \setminus L$. No assumption is made on $\Sigma$; Büchi's theorem and Vardi's Proposition 7 are stated for a finite nonempty alphabet.
nodes.title: Complement of an ω-regular language, over any alphabet

nodes.summary: For every finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton $A$ over an alphabet $\Sigma$, some finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton $\bar A$ satisfies $L_\omega(\bar A) = \Sigma^\omega \setminus L_\omega(A)$. No assumption is made on $\Sigma$, whereas the source works over a finite nonempty alphabet.
nodes.title: Büchi automata are closed under complementation

nodes.summary: For finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automata $A_1$ and $A_2$ over the same alphabet, some finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton $A$ satisfies $L_\omega(A) = L_\omega(A_1) \cap L_\omega(A_2)$.
nodes.title: Büchi automata are closed under intersection

nodes.summary: For finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automata $A_1$ and $A_2$ over the same alphabet, some finite-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton $A$ satisfies $L_\omega(A) = L_\omega(A_1) \cup L_\omega(A_2)$.
nodes.title: Büchi automata are closed under union

nodes.summary: There are Büchi automata $A_1$ and $A_2$ such that the plain product, with accepting set $F_1 \times F_2$, does not accept $L_\omega(A_1) \cap L_\omega(A_2)$. Vardi's example: both two-state cyclic automata accept $a^\omega$, but visit their accepting states at alternate instants, so their plain product is empty.
nodes.title: The plain product does not compute the intersection of Büchi languages

nodes.summary: Every infinite word accepted by the plain product of two Büchi automata over the same alphabet, with possibly different state types, is accepted by each of them: the components of an accepting product run are accepting runs of the two automata.
nodes.title: The plain product accepts only words in the intersection

nodes.summary: The plain product of the two-state cyclic automata with accepting sets $\{\mathsf{false}\}$ and $\{\mathsf{true}\}$ accepts no word: in the product run both components are in the same state at every instant, so they are never accepting at the same time.
nodes.title: Vardi's plain product is empty

nodes.summary: If its accepting set is nonempty, the two-state cyclic automaton accepts the only infinite word over its one-letter alphabet: its unique run alternates between the two states and so visits each of them infinitely often. With an empty accepting set it accepts nothing.
nodes.title: A two-state cyclic automaton with an accepting state accepts every word

nodes.summary: The plain product of Büchi automata $A_1$ and $A_2$ over the same alphabet (their state types may differ, within one universe) runs both synchronously on the input and has accepting set $F_1 \times F_2$: a run is accepting when both components are in accepting states at the same instants, infinitely often. It is the upstream CSLib product of automata over the index set $\{\mathsf{false}, \mathsf{true}\}$.
nodes.title: Plain product of two Büchi automata

nodes.summary: Over a one-letter alphabet, this Büchi automaton has states $\mathsf{false}$ (initial) and $\mathsf{true}$ and moves from each to the other at every step; its accepting set is a parameter. Vardi's automata $A_1$ and $A_2$ are the cases of accepting sets $\{\mathsf{false}\}$ and $\{\mathsf{true}\}$.
nodes.title: Two-state cyclic Büchi automaton
